claim:
For the antiferromagnetic two-qubit Heisenberg \(XX\) thermal channel of Yeo, let \(\eta=B_m/J\in[0,1)\), \(x_\eta=J/T_{\mathrm{tel}}(\eta)\), and let \(T_{\mathrm{tel}}(\eta)\) be the unique positive temperature at which the standard teleportation fidelity equals the classical threshold \(2/3\). Then \(x_\eta\) is the unique positive solution of
\[
\sinh x=\cosh(\eta x),
\]
equivalently
\[
\tanh\!\left(\frac{(1-\eta)x}{2}\right)=e^{-(1+\eta)x}.
\]
If \(W\) is the principal Lambert function, then as \(\eta\uparrow1\),
\[
x_\eta\sim\frac{W\!\left(2(1+\eta)/(1-\eta)\right)}{1+\eta},\qquad
\frac{T_{\mathrm{tel}}(\eta)}{J}\sim\frac{1+\eta}{W\!\left(2(1+\eta)/(1-\eta)\right)}
\sim\frac{2}{W\!\left(4/(1-\eta)\right)}.
\]
At that same operational threshold, the source concurrence has the exact form
\[
C_r(\eta)=\frac12-e^{-x_\eta}-\frac12e^{-2x_\eta},
\]
so \(C_r(\eta)\to1/2\) even though \(T_{\mathrm{tel}}(\eta)\to0\). More sharply,
\[
\frac12-C_r(\eta)\sim\frac12\sqrt{(1-\eta)\,W\!\left(4/(1-\eta)\right)}.
\]
Thus, approaching the field-driven level crossing \(B_m=J\) from below, the temperature window in which the unprocessed thermal state is useful for standard teleportation collapses only logarithmically, while the concurrence left at the classical-fidelity boundary rises to one half.

correctness.rationale: The source equality sinh(x)=cosh(eta x) is exactly equivalent to tanh((1-eta)x/2)=exp(-(1+eta)x), which proves uniqueness. Endpoint rescaling inverts through Lambert W. The source concurrence simplifies exactly at the threshold, giving the stated limit and gap asymptotic.
